questions.question: What is Received Pronunciation (RP)?
options: The prestige accent traditionally associated with the educated upper classes in England
The accent of the working class in Liverpool
The standard accent of American newsreaders
A dialect spoken only in Scotland
questions.explanation: RP, sometimes called "BBC English" or "the Queen's English", is the traditional prestige accent of England, associated with education and authority.

questions.question: What is a common alternative name for RP?
options: BBC English
Cockney
Estuary English
Geordie
questions.explanation: RP has been called "BBC English", "the Queen's English", and "Oxford English" because of its associations with broadcasting, royalty, and elite education.

questions.question: What is the American equivalent of the British word "lorry"?
options: Truck
Lift
Flat
Petrol
questions.explanation: British "lorry" corresponds to American "truck" - one of many everyday vocabulary differences between the two varieties.

questions.question: Why does British English remain influential worldwide despite America's dominance?
options: Its historical role as the original standard and its prestige in education and institutions
It has more speakers than American English
It is the only variety taught anywhere
British films dominate Hollywood
questions.explanation: As the historical standard, British English retains prestige in international education, examinations, and institutions across the former Empire.

questions.question: Is RP spoken by a majority of people in Britain?
options: No - only a small minority speak RP; most Britons have regional accents
Yes, nearly everyone speaks RP
Yes, it is legally required in schools
No, because RP is an American accent
questions.explanation: Despite its prestige, RP is spoken by only a small percentage of the British population; regional accents are the norm.
